data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's analogy to flocking birds misrepresents the coordination mechanism, and the disanalogy it acknowledges ('shared external signal is implicit/distributed') doesn't repair the fault. In a bird flock, synchrony arises from *direct local coupling* (sensory/motor) with negative-feedback dynamics that actively maintain coherence; in decentralized services coupled only through a market price, there is no closed-loop inter-agent feedback—each operator reacts to an aggregate statistic, not to each other. This undermines the 'functionally equivalent to a monolithic service' transfer claim because true phase-locking requires coupling that a broadcast price signal alone may not provide (prices aggregate information and can produce diverse quantity responses depending on cost structures, unlike direct sensory coupling). The analogy thus lends unwarranted strength to the 'crypto-correlated collapse' mechanism.
